definition: 19 exact ICRSP source articles directly opened and at least one identifiable passage per article inspected. No author-work or manuscript collation, complete panel survey, authoritative 1962 rubric verification or copyright clearance.

criticalSourceCorrections.issue: The site's 1606 sentence names Pope Paul VI, an impossible anachronism.
criticalSourceCorrections.correction: Pope Paul V reigned in 1606; corroborated independently by a Salesian-themed historical summary and secondary Catholic biographies.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Présentation: saint Martin's Tours/Candes biography, Roman cult diffusion and 1568 rank; Guéranger treats popular rural cult and conversion of pagan sacred sites.
rows.editorialBoundary: Do not accept the presentation's sweeping 'first non-martyr saint' characterization without historical qualification.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation describes cult recognition in 1606 and feast-date transfers; Guéranger introduces Gertrude's mystical writings.
rows.editorialBoundary: Source wrongly says Pope Paul VI in 1606; correct pontiff Paul V. Verify further chronology separately; do not confuse Gertrude the Great with Gertrude of Nivelles.

rows.sourceTitle: St Charles Borromée, évêque et confesseur
rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation dates death at Milan in 1580 and 1610 canonization; Guéranger develops Charles's Humilitas motto and pastoral reform.
rows.editorialBoundary: Historical rank changes are not instructions to modify the 1962 calendar.

rows.sourceTitle: St Augustin de Cantorbéry, évêque et confesseur
rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation traces Canterbury cult from the seventh century and Leo XIII's introduction of feast in 1882; Guéranger compares Eleutherius and Augustine in English evangelisation.
rows.editorialBoundary: Period-specific polemical descriptions of Anglicanism must not be reproduced as neutral history; distinct from St Augustine of Hippo.

rows.sourceTitle: Commémoraison de tous les Fidèles défunts
rows.observedSourceEvidence: Dom Lefèvre introductory passage connects All Saints and All Souls through the Communion of Saints and suffrages for the faithful departed; page identifies first Mass.
rows.editorialBoundary: Existing Requiem liturgical owner governs multiple Mass formulary contexts, not this introductory excerpt.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation recounts martyrdom of Josaphat Kuntsevych and nineteenth-century feast extension; Guéranger develops historical Eastern Catholic context.
rows.editorialBoundary: Host's union-and-schism rhetoric requires contextualisation; calendar and person identity must be matched first.

rows.sourceTitle: Présentation de la Bse Vierge Marie
rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation explicitly grounds Mary's presentation in apocryphal texts such as Protoevangelium of James and traces Western feast reception; Guéranger discusses hidden prayer.
rows.editorialBoundary: Do not portray a noncanonical infancy account as a Gospel fact; retain distinction between devotional tradition and canonical Scripture.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation explicitly says the historical vigil was suppressed in 1955; Guéranger relates Malachi, John the Baptist and Andrew to the approaching liturgical Advent.
rows.editorialBoundary: No reinstatement of pre-1955 vigil; Scripture references require exact lection ownership.

rows.sourceTitle: St Damase Ier, pape et confesseur
rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation recounts Damasus's Roman martyr cult and connection with Jerome; Guéranger links the pope's defense of Incarnation and Jerome's New Testament revision.
rows.editorialBoundary: Do not treat devotional literary descriptions as primary critical Jerome scholarship.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation distinguishes early attested Syracuse cult from uncertain historical details of her Passion; Guéranger discusses her name in Roman Canon and Advent imagery of light.
rows.editorialBoundary: Roman Canon invocation should be matched to existing Mass text; no new Mass reader cue.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Schuster describes Roman Friday Ember station at Holy Apostles and historic fasting; host explicitly says Guéranger supplied no separate commentary for each September Ember day.
rows.editorialBoundary: A generic shared Guéranger note is not three independently authored day commentaries; ancient historical practice is not automatically contemporary fasting obligation.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Schuster describes the ancient Saturday Ember vigil at St Peter's and the multiple readings; host says Guéranger's seasonal explanation is shared.
rows.editorialBoundary: Keep all Mass lesson sequences in their proper order and separate ancient nocturnal celebration from current 1962 practice.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Parsch explains the Christ the King feast through the Divine Office, Psalms and Colossians and its foundation under Pius XI.
rows.editorialBoundary: 1962 last-Sunday-of-October feast already owned by Calendar; don't build Office content.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation refers to suppressed 1955 Vigil; Guéranger interprets Andrew's witness and Cross at the threshold of Advent.
rows.editorialBoundary: Do not reinstate the vigil or conflate feast identity with historical preparation.

rows.sourceTitle: Fête-Dieu ou Fête du Très Saint Sacrement
rows.observedSourceEvidence: Site directs the reader elsewhere for longer commentary and its local presentation discusses Eucharistic sacrifice and the double consecration.
rows.editorialBoundary: Do not mark full commentaries read on this page; festival date does not automatically imply an actual procession.

rows.sourceTitle: Notre-Dame des Douleurs (Vendredi de la Passion)
rows.observedSourceEvidence: Guéranger describes Friday-in-Passiontide devotion to Mary's sorrows and the historical growth of the observance.
rows.editorialBoundary: Keep Marian formulary's edition/local status separate from the universal September Seven Sorrows feast; no duplicate module.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation identifies variable diocesan timing and a Nancy–Toul local proper; Guéranger notes diversity in date and Mass formulary.
rows.editorialBoundary: Do not invent universal Nov 5 feast; local rite/history and actual household custom remain different.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation cites seventh-century itineraries, a Domitilla-catacomb epitaph and transfer of relics to the Vatican in 757.
rows.editorialBoundary: The abbreviated inscription Mart. needs epigraphic scrutiny; do not conflate virgin and martyr categorisation or duplicate another Petronille source.

rows.observedSourceEvidence: Presentation distinguishes the pre-1955 Pentecost Vigil ceremonies from the 1960 Office alterations; Guéranger reflects older baptismal and fasting customs.
rows.editorialBoundary: Maintain strictly separate historic vigil readings and modern 1962 liturgical rubrics; Office descriptions remain archival.
